item.title: conduit clem
item.description: wow very crazy clem v smart phd type guy kinda like many of the arguments are somewhat hazy but pretty stronglow data big compute? many many params; strong regularization rl / fine tuning type more interesting loss functions / tasks for aneshtetics: power law to power proportional to 1/f^a compression (zip); how random is it critical field theory by annotating with that in mind you are biasing conduit has many ground truth taskstime domain fNIRS; time of flight of all the individual photons at very very high frequency can get distribution of time of flights -> moments 2d fNIRS has depth issue but the thesis (v much playing the long game): conventionally people believe volume conduction and gaussian blur for eeg & fNIRS; it is reasonable but like do you actually know specifically? basically "SNR is a construct" there is lots of noise but maybe the noise is correlated in non linear ways that current models cannot pick up on either due to architecetrue or lack of data eeg & fNIRS very easy and very developed; the hardware is right there for scaling and pretty studied + understood could not learn alg for intelligence with little data but with big data its easy similarly; in the beginning there was some progress with intel with curated statistical lms and rnns etc want to gather lots of data because power laws do the thing damn bro really has his shit down exactly when fNIRS helps v.s. doesnt help femto second laser; the detector that can detect singular photons and send electrical signal ofc short 500ms things fNIRS would be poor for and then longer time scale things fNIRS is better models overcoming deficits like line noise with more data want to stay agnostic and gather data in the most principled way instead of maximizing for information gain in the short term v bitter lesson when other modalities such as ultrasound become very strong they will defs get it (all of the stuff for what was said was not specific to EEG) can add inductive biases to make models better such as position encoding etc but can also not the job of the researchers is to collect the right data (use data attribution methods; 2nd order derivatives??) ensure the data is clean do cool ml to show findings generally the ml is something that companies will have to do anyways; doing alot of training and stuff on the big eeg will uncover what works and what doesnt & create a lot of latent knowledge (also infra for collecting data will be needed no matter what modality you need) notably multimodality has the benefit of the model being able to pick up on more interconnected signals that origins which we do not know about; at some point can run some interp but like not necessarily right now in response to "why not do better modality": "better" depends on goal if in the short term you want more signal yeah sure but for the long term when you are wanting ton consider bigger questions like consciousness and emergent behavior or very good foundation model which just straight up encodes brainstate losslessly across sessions & across subjects you might really want lots of data or multimodality shenanigans because human imposed restraints on what we are looking at may blind us from the true small scale interactions -> larger effects that are going on; who knows what it will look like so something like fUS is a different modality different tasks for the model such as: predict whether in the next 500ms they will press backspace predict fNIRS from EEG predict EEG from fNIRS hypothesis for smell (dam bro everyone has seen this #social ): the urgency for foul smells is much more than for pleasant smells and thus a whole lot of stim in random places should probably create much more foul smells on average but anyways some thoughts: the same location of stim on the olfactory bulb across people may create different sensations (its hard to pinpoint the OB anyways) thus will probably need to do some calibrations same thing for reading tbh different and pretty solid approach to neuroscience; has a lot of ml in itkernel headsetsbro the data collection setup is like a cave lol pretty scary people in those cells typing awaywent to cambridge and just did math cs physics; academic spongewants to participate in the fast moving history want to be great?

item.title: meditation calm after exercise; appreciating life bold
item.description:
meditation/calm after exercise; appreciating life #bold 22:52:52. march 18th, 2026 im biking through stanford on a downwards slope i rush through the wind like a runner full of adrenaline. i am full of adrenaline. speed makes me happy toward the station, i weave on the roads with not a car in sight down the ramp into the tunnel and out i come onto the station im exhausted but energetic i sit on a maroon bench on the south side of the north bound palo alto caltrain station sweating, i take off my glasses, and take my keys and phone out of my pockets. i unbuckle my helmet i plug in my front bike light and sit there while four drops of sweat slide slowly down the sides of my head i move my hands to wipe and then back nothing cars woosh by behind me i close my eyes. leaning into the 120 degree metal grid "back rest" hurts, do i dont instead, i sit up and breathe one deep breath is all that takse for me to become serene a deep sense of pleasure flows through my lungs into my body as i inhale bike light blue flashing; charging brick; backpack and bike and helmet and phone; four lamp posts on the other side with bright lights, unmoving; orange lights are evil twins. train arrives.
#A #experience
item.guid: ideaflow/2026-03-18/meditation calm after exercise; appreciating life bold.md

item.title: just hopped on a train, sat down, and just stared outside (d
item.description:
just hopped on a train, sat down, and just stared outside (dont usually do this, usually very always wanting to do work etc; though not in a bad way) i think i was a bit tired → getting some happy chemicals for sleep (melatonin?) and just chilled very distant from all of the things around me i really enjoyed that state of not being restrained by concerns etc this is probably what steven feels like everyday, just not really giving a f about too much stuff was thinking about how big the world really is, how every apartment in the complexes i was passing had a long long story of all the people in it, and how there are an (independently) estimated 10m-100m of these apartment buildings in the world, and how maybe 30-40% of the world is housed? connects to checkup! where i was like "rethink the goal of these"—i dont really care that much about the habits, i kinda just do whatever only bolt down on things i really care about, the rest shouldnt have that much effort put into them
